findings.message: The fallback `${_rc_disp:-interrupted}` fires only when `router_reason_disposition` returns empty — which only happens when `_rc_reason` is empty — but `_rc_reason` is always non-empty when `router_rc != 0`, making the fallback unreachable; if it ever fired, `interrupted` would be a semantically wrong disposition for an unknown failure reason (the catch-all from `router_reason_disposition` is `unavailable`, not `interrupted`); the same wrong fallback appears again on line 431 in the printf fallback path.

The else-branch of the v2 merge writes `impact_json` unchanged — with no `result_contract`, `disposition`, or `reason` fields — if jq fails on `. + {result_contract:2,...}`; in practice jq will not fail because `_impact_envelope_schema_ok` already validated the JSON, but unlike every other fallback write in this file (which spells out a full v2 `printf` literal), this else-branch silently produces a v1-only result that breaks the v2 contract guarantee; a matching v2 `printf` fallback like the one at line 430 would close the gap.

At every inline write site (lines 180, 433, 473, 560, 583, 623) `_IMPACT_RESULT_WRITTEN=1` is set unconditionally after the `||` fallback `printf`, even when both the jq+atomic_write and the printf fallback both failed (e.g. disk-full); the `_impact_write_result` helper is stricter — it sets the flag only inside the `if _json=... && atomic_write ...` success branch; if both writes fail at an inline site, the signal handler's guard reads `_IMPACT_RESULT_WRITTEN=1` and skips writing the interrupted result, leaving no result file on disk at all.
